title: I restyled my entire game, does the new look work?
author: room402games

comments.author: room402games
comments.body: Btw it's https://store.steampowered.com/app/4576460/Kingdom\_and\_Taxes/. There's an open playtest right now if you want to try the old version.

comments.author: Redditry199
comments.body:
lmao I just spent the last week on hex grid design for my game so it's funny to see this pop up.

The after is vastly improved thats for sure, but theres a big inconsistency - some building have black thick lines others have none, i think the oenes without look better but either way id recommend picking one and going with it.

replies.author: YumYumEatyTime
replies.body: Agreed, background and tiles are better with the update, but the black outlined graphics feel like they're overdoing the outlines

replies.author: room402games
replies.body: Yeah, agreed. The heavy outlines are on my list to tone down. Thanks!

replies.author: room402games
replies.body:
You're right, that inconsistency keeps coming up. Some buildings are placeholders with icons pulled from different sources, so the next step is exactly that: pick one consistent style and apply it everywhere.

Have you a link for your game ?

comments.author: Just-Investigator-20
comments.body: Am I the only one who likes things that are old?

comments.author: No_Elk_8930
comments.body:
Great progress:  
  
1.  The rock/gem to the building with columns is not clear to me.  Other items are scaled up for visibility I would suggest sizing that one up; or use a different icon that is more readable.

2.   Have you tried a version where the trade item icon comes out under the source building (as shown) and then arrives on top of the destination building (with a slow fade out on top of destination)?  That might read better as you get to see the item a little longer on its journey (if this is just background entertainment to the game then it is not necessary).

3.  The scroll/paper icon bothers me for some reason, maybe it is to attention grabbing because of relative color.

replies.author: room402games
replies.body: It's more of a roguelike city-builder where you have to build production chains to collect taxes. It's a single-player game.
